title: Understanding the Problem
text: The file is divided into $$8$$ blocks, each replicated twice. Each block is stored on $$2$$ out of $$4$$ machines. We need to determine the probability that the file can still be read if $$2$$ machines fail.

title: Analyzing Block Storage
text: Each block is stored on $$2$$ machines. If $$2$$ machines fail, a block can still be read if at least one of its replicas is on one of the remaining machines.

title: Calculating Probability for One Block
text: For a single block, calculate the probability that at least one replica is on the remaining machines. Consider the combinations of machine selections.

title: Probability of Block Being Readable
text: Calculate the probability that a block is still readable if $$2$$ machines fail. Use the fact that each block is stored on $$2$$ machines.

title: Extending to All Blocks
text: Since there are $$8$$ blocks, and each block's readability is independent, use the probability for one block to find the probability for all blocks.

title: Final Probability Calculation
text: Calculate the probability that all $$8$$ blocks are readable, given the probability for one block.
